native.answer:
After a vasectomy, the sperm continue to be produced in the testicles. However, because the vas deferens – the tubes that carry sperm – have been cut and sealed, the sperm can no longer travel out of the body in semen.

The body naturally absorbs the sperm. White blood cells essentially break down and dissolve the sperm over time. This process isn’t harmful and doesn’t cause any build-up or health problems. There might be a slight back-up initially, causing some temporary discomfort or swelling, but this usually resolves on its own. The testicles continue functioning as normal, producing sperm, but the sperm are reabsorbed by the body.
